questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available at the chosen university were the most crucial factors for my choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think, that if I would do exchange again. I would focus more on the location and also on the time of year. Since it turned out that the courses I wanted to take were not available for me and most of the courses I took not as challenging than the once at my home university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university McMaster had made most of the information very clear to exchange and international students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had an introduction on my first day and throughout the semester events for international and exchange students in which I often participated

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have liked to have an exchange buddy. Since I was very difficult to get to know the Canadians.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I had a nice, but way to expensive room shared with another student. I was lucky though a lot of the stories about other on campus accommodations were horrible.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I was forced to have a meal plan. Even though a kitchen was available. The food on campus was way to expensive..

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't live on campus even though it seems easier. It is not worth the money and (at my university) no community were created for the people living there. Also people are way younger.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been such a long time, that I don't really remember.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Too long ago.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An information book and also I could email the university and they answered.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very much. I only found out later that there were courses I wasn't allowed to take without it being announced somewhere. (The courses were the main reasons for my choice).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The boards main focus seems to be to make money of the students instead of giving them the best education. Also they invest in fossil fuels and are building natural gas generators on campus without listening to the protests from students, professors and other people working at the institution.
https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/mcmaster-divestment-project-hunger-strike-ends-1.6793248

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not as challenging as on my home institution. The only course I found nice was about quantum information.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less teaching. Courses way shorter. A lot more assignments

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Exploration in medical and biological physics
Modelling life 
Quantum information and computation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Quantum information and computation by Duncan O'dell.
A nice course to that goes through a lot of different applications of quantum mechanics while also creating a better understanding of the concepts.

questions.answer: Canada is an extremely expensive country.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many opportunities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym, Swimmingpool, a lot of clubs, orkestras etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you like. I enjoyed taking part in hikes with the outdoor club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are so many hikes around the area. I recommend just exploring Hamilton and the nature and also Toronto. Everything else is way to far away for a weekend trip. Bruce Peninsula! And blue mountains!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took along time to get Canadian friends

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Living on campus.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Lots of people live to hike and Canadians are very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I recommend going in the summer. 
Don't live on campus. 
Explore the area around.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to do a lot of assignments and very short lectures.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a part of the country and some of its history. Also meeting so many students from other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The winter without snow.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
